title: Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present on OIDC logout with AWS cognito
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary While using st.logout() with AWS cognito configured over OIDC in the secrets.toml, the error is returned ``` Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present ``` The url is then ``` https://2015-40786-user-productflight.auth.eu-west-1.amazoncognito.com/error?client_id=5ceho48rc7uuvf044cl8okc6v1&post_logout_redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2F2015-40786.cockpit.productflight.io%2Foauth2callback&id_token_hint=... ``` The log out is happening though, if you press back and return to the root app, the user is logged out. Is post_logout_redirect_uri the culprit? ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python secrets.toml... [auth] redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8501/oauth2callback" cookie_secret = "123" client_id = "xxx" client_secret = "yyy" server_metadata_url = "https://cognito-idp.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/eu-west-1_B5Zn6WAh4/.well-known/openid-configuration" streamlit... if st.user.is_logged_in: if st.button("Logout", key="logout", type="tertiary"): logout() return st.login() ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Login with the OIDC AWS Cognito configured 2. Logout 3. See error 4. Press back button in the browser 5. User logged out ### Expected Behavior User logged out and redirected to the login screen ### Current Behavior _No response_ ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version:1.55.0 - Python version:3.12.11 - Operating System: Ubuntu 22 - Browser: chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14601)

This is a bug in the OIDC logout flow when using AWS Cognito as the identity provider. The root cause is in `build_logout_url()` in [`lib/streamlit/auth_util.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/auth_util.py#L223-L226), which constructs the logout URL using the standard OIDC RP-Initiated Logout parameter name `post_logout_redirect_uri`. However, AWS Cognito's logout endpoint does **not** follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout specification — it expects the parameter to be named `redirect_uri` (or `logout_uri`) instead. When Streamlit sends `post_logout_redirect_uri`, Cognito rejects it with "Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present". The logout itself still succeeds server-side (cookies are cleared before the redirect), which is why pressing the browser back button shows the user as logged out.

A potential fix would be to either detect Cognito-style endpoints and use the appropriate parameter name, or to allow users to configure custom logout parameters for non-standard providers.

### Related Issues

- **#12144** ([st.logout() doesn't redirect to correct Cognito ESE](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12144)) — CLOSED. Very similar Cognito logout issue from v1.48.0 where `client_id` was missing from the logout URL. Fixed via revert in 1.48.1, but the underlying Cognito parameter naming incompatibility (`post_logout_redirect_uri` vs `redirect_uri`) was not addressed.
- **#12169** ([Breaking Change: Streamlit 1.48 breaks st.logout()](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12169)) — CLOSED. Related regression where `post_logout_redirect_uri` caused errors with Auth0 as well, confirming that multiple providers have non-standard logout parameter expectations.
- **#11703** ([Allow advanced customization of OIDC/OAuth2 parameters in st.login()](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11703)) — OPEN. Enhancement request for customizable OIDC parameters that could serve as a workaround for provider-specific logout parameter requirements.

## Reproduction Assessment: **CONFIRMED** (via code analysis)

This bug is confirmed real. I was unable to do a live reproduction (no Cognito user pool available), but the root cause is unambiguous from the source code.

### Root Cause

In [`lib/streamlit/auth_util.py:223-226`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/auth_util.py#L223-L226), `build_logout_url()` hardcodes the OIDC standard parameter name `post_logout_redirect_uri`:

```python
logout_params: dict[str, str] = {
    "client_id": client_id,
    "post_logout_redirect_uri": post_logout_redirect_uri,
}
```

AWS Cognito's logout endpoint does **not** follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout spec. It requires `redirect_uri` (or `logout_uri`), not `post_logout_redirect_uri`. It also ignores `id_token_hint`.

So Streamlit sends: `?client_id=...&post_logout_redirect_uri=...&id_token_hint=...`
But Cognito expects: `?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...`

This matches the exact error reported: *"Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present"*

### Why logout still works

The server-side logout (cookie clearing) happens **before** the redirect to the provider's logout endpoint. So the Streamlit session is invalidated regardless of whether the provider redirect succeeds — which is why pressing back shows the user as logged out.

### Scope

This likely affects any OIDC provider whose `end_session_endpoint` doesn't follow the RP-Initiated Logout spec parameter naming. Related: #12169 showed Auth0 had the same issue.

A potential fix would be to allow users to configure custom logout query parameters, or to detect non-standard providers and adjust the parameter name accordingly.

Hey! The diagnosis here seems right. Cognito's logout endpoint doesn't follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout spec and expects `redirect_uri` instead of `post_logout_redirect_uri`.

I put together a draft PR (#14868) that adds an optional `[auth.logout_params]` section to secrets.toml so you can override the default parameter names. For Cognito it'd look like:

```toml
[auth.logout_params]
redirect_uri_name = "redirect_uri"
include_id_token_hint = false
```

Still needs a more thorough review/approval but wanted to get it out there. Would love to know if the config shape makes sense for your use case.
Going to close this as a duplicate of #14290. We can continue conversation there.
